steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Crash desk leftover is /app/bin/clatter (native ELF, first bytes \x7fELF). Load the well with tallow, emit the upload with pour. Outputs are /app/kegbay/upload.json and /app/kegbay/batch.tsv. Modules named in /app/opsheet/ROUTE.txt are the pipeline to correct under /app. Static copies of the keg files are not enough. Finish with a compiled ELF at /app/bin/clatter. The test pipeline reruns /app/bin/clatter tallow then /app/bin/clatter pour.

Unchanged /app/dropwell still has the same files on disk. Remaining keg rows keep correct checksums and batch_count tracks the row count, but some well names never appear on the keg, seq permutes, and a re-upload disagrees with /app/tidearc/lastgood.rec. Fresh-process mint must byte-match the previous keg pair. Names that exist in both the well and last-good stay in the same order relative to each other as in last-good. seq is 1..n for the current well and may shift when new dumps appear. Order follows dump clocks and companion grouping in /app/opsheet/FORMAT.txt. If last-good is absent, sequence still comes from those dump fields. Each well file shows up once. digest is lowercase hex of the full dump bytes using the hash named in /app/opsheet/FORMAT.txt.

Keg JSON/TSV columns, MARK polarity, and pour root rules live in /app/opsheet/FORMAT.txt. upload.json entries carry seq, name, digest, and guid with batch_count. Success writes /app/kegbay/MARK as ok. Empty well, or /app/bin/clatter pour /app/scratch outside /app/dropwell, exits nonzero. On failure /app/kegbay/MARK must not exist; a false body is not the failure signal.


Current terminal state:
Current Terminal Screen:
root@45d1eb709689:/app#

Analysis: We are at /app with no inspection performed yet. We need read ROUTE.txt and FORMAT.txt, identify the named source modules, inspect the existing ELF/build setup and fixture files, then repair and compile clatter.
Plan: First inspect the operation specifications, repository layout, executable metadata, source/build files, current keg outputs, and last-good record. This will establish the required formats and implementation language before making changes.

arguments.keystrokes:
printf '%s
' '--- ROUTE ---'; cat /app/opsheet/ROUTE.txt; printf '%s
' '--- FORMAT ---'; cat /app/opsheet/FORMAT.txt; printf '%s
' '--- TREE ---'; find /app -maxdepth 3 -type f -printf '%p
' | sort

printf '%s
' '--- ELF ---'; file /app/bin/clatter; printf '%s
' '--- BUILD/SOURCES ---'; find /app -maxdepth 3 -type f \( -name 'Makefile' -o -name '*.c' -o -name '*.h' -o -name '*.cc' -o -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.rs' \) -print -exec sed -n '1,240p' {} \;; printf '%s
' '--- LASTGOOD ---'; test -f /app/tidearc/lastgood.rec && cat /app/tidearc/lastgood.rec || true; printf '%s
' '--- CURRENT KEG ---'; for f in /app/kegbay/upload.json /app/kegbay/batch.tsv /app/kegbay/MARK; do echo "[$f]"; test -e "$f" && cat "$f" || echo MISSING; done

printf '%s
' '--- DROPWELL ---'; find /app/dropwell -maxdepth 2 -type f -printf '%P	%s bytes	%TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM:%TS
' | sort; printf '%s
' '--- FILE SAMPLES ---'; for f in /app/dropwell/*; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; echo "### $f"; file "$f"; head -c 256 "$f" | xxd; done
